clue.text: Favourite article — quite missing it in game

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, as in teacher's pet
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: missing tells us the word it is taken out of the word quite, leaving what remains

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost a favourite item feels it is quite missing from their game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing it' takes IT out of QUITE, leaving QUE, which follows PET and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pétanque is a French bowls game played with metal balls on gravel.

clue.text: Unnaturally satisfied with trees coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gums are gum trees, eucalyptus

explanation.surface: Someone oddly pleased as trees grow up around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns GUMS (gum trees) upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A complacent person is pleased with themselves beyond what is warranted.

clue.text: Sportsman, one receiving start of rally

parts.note: a fence is a person who receives stolen goods

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the word rally

explanation.surface: A sportsman who catches the opening shot of a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is slang for a receiver of stolen goods; the first letter of 'rally' follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer competes in the sport of swordplay with foil, épée or sabre.

clue.text: Primate supporting justice's prank

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other one

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for justice, a judge's title
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey backing up a judge's practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supporting' puts APE below J.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or playful trick.

clue.text: Holiday time? Remote ocean's feasible

parts.note: the high seas are the open ocean far from any coast
something feasible is on, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A traveller judges that crossing a distant ocean is possible in holiday time.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as HIGH SEAS + ON; the question mark marks a definition by example, the busiest season for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak tourist period of the year is when most people take their vacations.

clue.text: He painted entry, leaving it unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for entry loses its last letter

parts.note: ingress means entry or the act of going in

explanation.surface: An artist finds the way in left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving it unfinished' drops the final S of INGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical artist of portraits and nudes.

clue.text: What I'll make the girl 1 I adore, accepting love — this girl?

indicators.note: accepting means the phrase takes a letter inside it

parts.words: What I'll make the girl 1 I adore
parts.note: a lover vows to make her mine, so this phrase gives the two words her and mine; the 1 is a stray print mark
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A suitor wonders what he will make of the girl he adores, and whether she is the one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts O (love) inside HER MINE. The definition is a girl's name, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, borne by the queen in The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Precisely where the hammer lands

definitions.meaning: the spot struck when a carpenter drives a nail

explanation.definitionFit: Paying on the nail means paying exactly and at once; literally, a hammer strikes the head of a nail.

clue.text: Friends from Paris taking in northern French city

indicators.note: taking in means the French word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: amies is French for female friends

explanation.surface: Parisian friends visit a city in the north of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts N inside AMIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is the capital of the Somme department, famous for its Gothic cathedral.

clue.text: Peculiar jargon covering end of Perpendicular and start of Gothic

annotationWithheld.why: 'Peculiar jargon covering end of Perpendicular and start of Gothic' (5): R and G are named, but no clue words give the remaining A, O, T around them; the clue as held seems misread or incomplete.

clue.text: County game curtailed — Hampshire's opener's anger

indicators.note: curtailed means the game loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, here of Hampshire

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: A county game cut short when Hampshire's opening batsman loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts CHESS to CHES; 'opener' gives the H of Hampshire. Hampshire is an English county with a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is an English county in the north-west, home of the cheese.

clue.text: Independent doesn't let I them present the figures at the end

definitions.text: Independent doesn't let I them present the figures at the end

parts.words: Independent doesn't let I them present the figures at the end
parts.note: the Independent newspaper prints each clue's letter count in round brackets, not the angular kind; the stray I is a print mark

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor refuses to let someone report the final figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' is the newspaper this puzzle comes from; the 'figures at the end' are the letter counts after each clue, which it encloses in round brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Typographical marks with right-angled corners used to enclose text, an alternative to parentheses.

clue.text: Star actor I recast as nobleman

indicators.note: recast means the letters of star actor I are thrown into a new arrangement, as a play is recast

explanation.surface: A theatre star is replaced in a role as a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recast' rearranges STAR ACTOR I.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristocrat is a member of the titled upper class, a peer.

clue.text: Represented as ice-free when heat is off, say

indicators.note: represented here means presented again in a new form, so the letters of as ice-free are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something shown as free of ice once the heating is turned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' (re-presented) rearranges AS ICE-FREE. 'Heat' is the heat of battle, so the definition describes a truce; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a moment when fighting stops, when the heat of battle is turned off.

clue.text: Oratorio, I judge, in sound being revolutionary

indicators.note: in means the letters I and J go inside the turned word
being revolutionary means the word for sound is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: hale means sound, healthy

explanation.surface: An oratorio judged as healthy and radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being revolutionary' turns HALE into ELAH; 'in' puts I and J inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is Mendelssohn's oratorio about the Old Testament prophet.

clue.text: Lawyers leading social group in fictitious county 4

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
a set is a social circle

explanation.surface: Lawyers head the local society of an imaginary shire.
explanation.walkthrough: Barset is Trollope's imaginary county, the setting of his Barsetshire novels; the 4 after it is a stray print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope invented this English shire for his Victorian novels of cathedral life.

clue.text: Value in varying rate for certain

indicators.note: varying means the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A rate that varies is certain to affect value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varying' rearranges RATE to TREA, followed by SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to prize it highly.

clue.text: Leprechauns, possibly — 5 or creatures from further away?

definitions.meaning: Irish fairies are small and dressed in green
beings from outer space, the usual cartoon martians

explanation.walkthrough: The 5 in the clue is a stray print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Small green-clad fairies fit the phrase literally, while in popular culture it names imagined aliens from other planets.

clue.text: Prominent orchestral player in radio broadcast for songs

indicators.note: a radio broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the leader of an orchestra is its principal first violin

explanation.surface: A star of the orchestra appears in a radio programme of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in radio broadcast' says LEADER is heard, giving the German word for songs; in Britain the orchestra's leader is its first violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Pop music's rubbish — no hint of brains

indicators.note: no means a letter is taken away from the word for rubbish

parts.note: garbage means rubbish

indicators.note: hint of picks out the first letter of brains

explanation.surface: A critic calls a kind of pop music mindless rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hint of' gives B, the first letter of 'brains'; 'no' takes that B out of GARBAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage is a style of electronic dance music from the 1990s.

clue.text: It's needed for warmth when going out

definitions.text: It's needed for warmth when going out

parts.words: It's needed for warmth when going out
parts.note: sounds like a coat for a trip outdoors, but going out here means falling asleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' suggests leaving the house; it means going out like a light, dropping off to sleep in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt or blanket keeps a sleeper warm through the night.

clue.text: Swerve, always half twisted

indicators.note: half twisted means only the first half of the word for always is turned round

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A car swerves and is always partly spun round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half twisted' reverses the first half of EVER, EV becoming VE, then ER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to change direction suddenly.

clue.text: River accounting for more than half of activity?

indicators.note: more than half of means the word for activity is cut short, keeping five of its eight letters

parts.note: industry is busy activity, diligence

explanation.surface: A river responsible for most of the region's commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half of' keeps the first five letters of INDUSTRY, dropping TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is the great river of Pakistan, flowing from Tibet to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Consumed cocktail, say, ignoring recipe that's unpleasantly wet

indicators.note: ignoring means a letter is left out of the word for consumed

parts.note: to drink a cocktail or any other beverage is to have drank it; drank means consumed liquid
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a cocktail without following the recipe and finds it soggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' takes R (recipe) out of DRANK.
explanation.definitionFit: Dank describes a damp, cold and musty place.

clue.text: Period when tapestries

annotationWithheld.why: 'Period when tapestries' (6): the clue as held is cut short; SEW + AGE fits the words, but no definition of the answer survives.

clue.text: Lots of plants about to be involved in recycling of energy

indicators.note: to be involved in means the short word goes inside the other letters
recycling of means the letters of energy are reprocessed into a new order

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Plants about to be part of an energy recycling scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling of' rearranges ENERGY, and 'to be involved in' puts RE inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage or vegetation collectively.
